lines.en: It is often said that when the rich world catches a cold, the poor world gets pneumonia.
What worries economists is not the debt itself, but the speed at which it is growing.
Not until prices began to fall did families feel any relief from the crisis.
However strong a currency may seem, it rests on nothing but the trust of those who use it.
The price of bread is said to affect political stability more than any election speech.
Were trade between countries to stop tomorrow, the shelves of our shops would empty within weeks.
It is not wealth that makes a country stable, but the fairness with which that wealth is shared.
Little attention is paid to small businesses, even though they employ most of the country.
What history shows is that every economic crisis eventually ends, though not everyone recovers equally.
Rarely do economists agree on anything, yet they all warn against ignoring inflation.
What the crisis exposed was how dependent the whole economy had become on a single source of income.
It is when people lose trust in their currency that saving becomes impossible for ordinary families.
Only when exports began to rise did the government speak openly about the depth of the problem.
Were interest rates to rise again this year, many small businesses would close their doors for good.
It is not the size of an economy that determines its strength, but its ability to adapt to shocks.
